edges.description: Inactivated macrophages do not mature into the epithelioid and giant cells of an organised granuloma; this applies to complete deficiency.
Macrophages that cannot be activated by IFN-gamma also fail to control intracellular Salmonella, but this is far less frequent in IFN-gammaR1 deficiency than mycobacterial disease.

Persisting mycobacterial burden keeps the IL-12 to IFN-gamma circuit running. Infected phagocytes release IL-12, which induces IFN-gamma from T and NK cells; that arm is intact here, so IFN-gamma accumulates with no receptor to act on it.

edges.description: Granulomas that do not contain the bacilli fail to restrict their spread, and lepromatous-like granulomas go with the very severe outcome of complete deficiency.

edges.description: A receptor-null mouse reproduces the lesion of complete deficiency without detectable surface receptor, and shows that loss of the receptor impairs innate resistance without disturbing immune development.
edges.limitations: The cited study challenged the mice with Listeria and vaccinia, not with BCG or environmental mycobacteria, so it does not show the mycobacterial phenotype that defines the human disease. A null allele models only the complete form without surface receptor; it says nothing about the surface-expressed non-binding form or the partial form.

nodes.description: IFN-gammaR1 is the ligand-binding chain of the receptor. In most cases of complete deficiency no receptor is detectable at the cell surface; in the surface-expressed complete form the receptor is present in normal amounts but its IFN-gamma-binding site is disrupted. Either way the receptor binds no ligand. In partial recessive deficiency the receptor is expressed but responds only to high IFN-gamma concentrations, and with the M1K allele normal receptor is made at low levels by leaky translation initiation.

nodes.description: Germline biallelic IFNGR1 variants of several molecular classes. Most complete-deficiency alleles are nonsense, frameshift or splice variants that introduce a premature stop codon upstream of the transmembrane segment; in-frame deletions and missense variants in the extracellular domain, whole-gene deletions and compound heterozygosity for a copy-number variant are rarer. The partial recessive alleles are the I87T and V63G missense founder variants and the M1K initiation-codon variant.

evidence.snippet: Most of the autosomal recessive IFNGR1 mutations are homozygous loss-of-function single-nucleotide variants, whereas large genomic deletions and compound heterozygosity have been very rarely reported.

evidence.snippet: A 119.227 nt homozygous deletion on chromosome 6q23.3 was identified, removing the IFNGR1 gene completely and ending 117 nt upstream of the transcription start of the IL22RA2 gene.

nodes.description: IFN-gamma is the signal that activates macrophages to kill intracellular mycobacteria. Without it macrophages fail to up-regulate TNF-alpha and do not acquire mycobactericidal activity. How far this step fails tracks the residual IFN-gamma response, which is why the complete and partial forms differ in severity.

nodes.description: The only curative treatment for complete deficiency. Graft rejection and delayed engraftment are common, even with HLA-identical donors, and are attributed to high plasma IFN-gamma; outcomes are better when infection is controlled and IFN-gamma has normalised before transplant. Not indicated in the milder partial forms; the one patient with the severe M1K partial form was transplanted.

nodes.description: Specific to complete deficiency (subtype AR complete). Without IFN-gamma-activated macrophages, granulomas are poorly delimited, lack epithelioid and multinucleated giant cells, and are multibacillary (lepromatous-like). Partial recessive deficiency instead forms mature tuberculoid granulomas, and the severe M1K partial form shows no granulomatous reaction at all. Failure to wall off the infection is part of why disease disseminates in the complete form.

The defect is absolute in complete deficiency and dose-dependent in partial deficiency, where cells respond only at high IFN-gamma concentrations.

nodes.description: Macrophages that are not activated by IFN-gamma cannot clear ingested mycobacteria, so weakly virulent environmental species and BCG replicate inside them and disseminate to lymph nodes, liver, spleen, bone and other organs. The burden is highest in complete deficiency, where lesions are multibacillary; residual receptor function in the partial form limits it.
